value.rationale: The exact crossing and two opposite rational witnesses show that a standard static predator reproduction benchmark can misclassify invasion in *both* directions under an attracting oscillating resident prey population. This resolves a motivated model-specific dynamical boundary using exact algebra and positive-matrix Floquet theory, rather than numerical examples alone.

final_claim: In a fixed positive subfamily of a discrete prey–juvenile/adult predator Euler map, the attracting predator-free prey two-cycle has a rare-predator Floquet threshold whose comparison to the carrying-capacity static index reverses exactly at counterattack A=2/35 along R_static=1; two exact rational witnesses show both strict directions.
limitations: Only one explicit positive Euler parameter subfamily; local linearized invasion, not global predator persistence.
